title: Limits
goal: See where a graph is heading as $x$ gets right next to a target number from the left and right—even if there is a hole or a jump right at that spot.

beforeThis.skill: Quick check: an open circle $\circ$ on a graph means "missing point (hole)," while a filled dot $\bullet$ shows the actual plugged-in height $f(a)$.

questions.asking: Find the height the curve approaches as $x$ gets close to $-2$, $0$, and $2$ from both sides, or state if the limit does not exist.
questions.statement:
Given the function shown below, evaluate the following:

  1. $\lim_{x \to -2} f(x)$
  2. $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$
  3. $\lim_{x \to 2} f(x)$

figures.alt: Coordinate axes showing the graph of y = f(x). As x approaches -2 from both sides, the curve rises to a peak at y = 1. The curve passes smoothly through the origin (0, 0). As x approaches 2 from both sides, the curve levels off at an open circle at (2, 2), while a separate filled dot is plotted at (2, -2).

questions.asking: Check if the left-hand and right-hand heights of the curve agree as $x$ approaches $0$, and give that common value or state that the limit does not exist.
questions.statement: Given the function shown below, evaluate $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$.

figures.alt: Coordinate axes showing a piecewise graph y = f(x) with a jump at x = 0. From the left (x < 0), the curve approaches an open circle at (0, -1). At x = 0 and to the right (x >= 0), the curve starts at a filled dot at (0, 1) and rises smoothly for positive x.

questions.asking: Read five one-sided or two-sided limits from the piecewise linear graph by following the appropriate branch toward each target $x$-value.
questions.statement:
Given the function shown below, evaluate:

  1. $\lim_{x \to -1^-} f(x)$
  2. $\lim_{x \to -1^+} f(x)$
  3. $\lim_{x \to -1} f(x)$
  4. $\lim_{x \to -2^+} f(x)$
  5. $\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x)$

figures.alt: Coordinate axes showing y = f(x) made of three parallel line segments with open circles at all endpoints: the first segment goes from (-2, 0) to (-1, 2); the second goes from (-1, -2) through (0, 0) to (1, 2); the third goes from (1, -2) to (2, 0).

questions.asking: Check if knowing the limit of $f(x)$ as $x$ approaches $3$ forces the actual function value $f(3)$ to equal that same number.
Find the value of the left-hand limit at $x = -2$ when you already know the two-sided limit at $x = -2$ equals $16$.
questions.statement: Suppose $f(x)$ is a function defined on all real numbers, and $\lim_{x \to -2} f(x) = 16$. What is $\lim_{x \to -2^-} f(x)$?

questions.asking: See what height $\sin t$ approaches as the angle $t$ shrinks to $0$ radians on the unit circle.
See what happens to the natural logarithm $\log x$ as $x$ approaches $0$ through positive numbers.
See what number $y^2$ gets close to as $y$ gets right next to $3$ (since $y^2$ has no holes or jumps, you can just plug in $y = 3$).
See what happens to $1/x$ when you divide $1$ by a tiny negative number (like $-0.0001$) as $x \to 0^-$.
Check if the two-sided limit of $1/x$ at $x = 0$ exists by comparing the behaviour on both sides of $0$.
See what happens to $1/x^2$ when you divide $1$ by a tiny positive number $x^2$ as $x \to 0$ from either side.
Find the height of the flat horizontal line $y = 1/10$ as $x$ approaches $3$ (a constant never changes height!).
Find the value that $f(x)$ approaches as $x$ gets very close to $3$ by checking which rule applies immediately around $x = 3$.
questions.statement:
Evaluate $\lim_{x \to 3} f(x)$, where

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \sin x & x \le 2.9 \\ x^2 & x > 2.9 \end{cases}$$
